subject: Notice of Electronic Filing: Case 26-CV-04417
body: A document has been filed in the above-referenced case: Order Setting Case Management Conference. Parties shall file a joint statement no later than fourteen (14) days before the conference date of October 20, 2026.
note: An automated e-filing notice like twenty others this month, the deadline buried in the second sentence. The joint statement is due October 6, but it is written as fourteen days before the conference, which code does not count backwards from, so the managing partner sets the date.

subject: Okonkwo: Defendant's First Set of Interrogatories
body: Please find attached Defendant Brightline Logistics' First Set of Interrogatories and Requests for Production of Documents to Plaintiff Marcus Okonkwo, served today by electronic mail per the parties' agreement. Responses are due within thirty (30) days of service.
note: Served discovery with its window stated. A plain service cover note asks nothing else, so it is discovery only, not opposing counsel correspondence.

subject: Any news?
body: Hi, just checking in again. Has anything happened with my case since we last spoke? I haven't heard back on my message from last week.
note: A second unanswered message from the client on an active matter.

subject: Wrongful termination: looking for representation
body: I was let go last month after reporting safety issues and I think it was retaliation. Are you taking new cases? I can send documents.
note: No date anywhere, but a retaliation claim can carry an administrative filing window measured in weeks. The clock runs with no date, so a person establishes it.

from: Dr. Helen Park, Park Forensic Economics
subject: Invoice 0912: expert analysis, Okonkwo
body: Attached is our invoice for the damages analysis and report preparation in Okonkwo v. Brightline. Terms net 30.
note: An expert's bill against the Okonkwo matter.

subject: Meet and confer: protective order
body: Following up on my voicemail. Can we find 30 minutes this week to discuss the scope of the protective order before we bring it to the court?
note: Opposing counsel asking a second time, after a voicemail. No date attached.

subject: Cut research time in half: 30-day trial
body: Litigators at firms your size are saving hours a week. Start a free trial today.

subject: Ethics credit deadline approaching
body: Reminder: your compliance period ends January 31. Register now for our fall ethics series.
note: Sounds like the bar, reads like a compliance reminder, and sells a seminar. A real date, but not a matter deadline.

subject: Conference room B booked Thursday
body: I've got the room from 1 to 4 for the Okonkwo document review. Bring the second box.

subject: Returned filing: Case 26-CV-03980
body: Your filing has been rejected for a missing certificate of service. Corrected filings must be resubmitted within 5 court days to retain the original filing date.
note: A returned filing with a cure window in court days.

subject: Activity in Case 25-CV-11862 Delgado v. Marlow Foods: Scheduling Order
body:
This is an automatic e-mail message generated by the CM/ECF system. The following transaction was entered on 9/15/2026.

SCHEDULING ORDER. Amended pleadings due by October 30, 2026. Expert disclosures due by November 20, 2026. Discovery closes January 15, 2027. Dispositive motions to be filed no later than February 12, 2027. Signed by Magistrate Judge Corinne Albright.
note: A scheduling order sets several dates; the first one stated is the one the parser reads, and the rest go on the docket by hand. A dated court item is never below high.

subject: Notice of Hearing: Case 26-CV-03980
body: Defendant Tillery Construction's Motion to Compel Arbitration is set for hearing on October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. in Department 14. Remote appearances are permitted through the court's video platform.
note: A hearing notice is a calendar entry, not a response clock. The opposition it implies is already on the docket.

subject: Notice of Electronic Filing: Case 26-CV-04417 Order on Stipulation
body: A document has been filed in the above-referenced case: Order Granting Stipulation to Continue Hearing. The hearing on Plaintiff's Motion for Leave to File a First Amended Complaint is continued to November 4, 2026 at 9:00 a.m.
note: A continuance moves a hearing; nothing new is owed.

subject: Activity in Case 25-CV-11862: Order on Motion to Compel
body:
The following transaction was entered on 9/18/2026.

ORDER granting in part Plaintiff's Motion to Compel Further Responses to Requests for Production. Defendant shall serve supplemental responses and produce responsive documents within twenty (20) days of this order. Requests for fees are denied without prejudice.
note: A court order on a discovery motion is a court notice, with its own window.

subject: Activity in Case 25-CV-11862: Order to Show Cause
body:
The following transaction was entered on 9/19/2026.

ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE why sanctions should not issue for failure to appear at the September 10 status conference. Counsel for Defendant shall file a written response no later than October 2, 2026. Hearing on the order set for October 9, 2026.
note: An order to show cause with a written response date.

subject: Notice of Reassignment: Case 26-CV-04417
body: Please take notice that the above case has been reassigned for all purposes to the Honorable Leonard Ellery, Department 22, effective immediately. All previously scheduled dates remain on calendar. A party who has not exercised a peremptory challenge may do so within fifteen (15) days of service of this notice.
note: An administrative reassignment notice that reads as housekeeping. The challenge window in its last sentence is a real clock.

subject: Filing Accepted: Envelope 41893317
body: Your filing in Case 26-CV-03980, Plaintiff Vance Holdings LLC's Case Management Statement, has been accepted by the clerk. A conformed copy is attached.
note: The firm's own filing, accepted. Court mail with nothing owed.

subject: Filing fee deficiency: Case 26-CV-03980
body: The motion submitted on September 16 was received with an insufficient filing fee. The balance of $60.00 must be paid within 10 days of this notice or the motion will be stricken from the calendar.
note: A fee problem the court raises is a court notice, not a bill. It carries a cure window.

subject: Notice of Electronic Filing: Case 26-CV-03980 Trial Setting Order
body: A document has been filed in the above-referenced case: Trial Setting Order. Jury trial is set for March 8, 2027. The final status conference is set for February 19, 2027. Counsel are directed to the department's trial procedures on the court website.
note: Dates on a calendar, none of them a response the firm owes now.

subject: Delgado v. Marlow Foods: Plaintiff's Third Set of Interrogatories
body: Counsel, attached is Plaintiff's Third Set of Interrogatories to Defendant Marlow Foods Inc., served today via e-service (transaction 41845901). Please direct any questions to me.
note: The tracker already has the set. The plaintiff's deposition on September 30 waits on discovery and falls before the response date, so the schedule makes it urgent.

subject: Notice of Deposition: Renata Solis
body: Please see the attached Notice of Deposition of Renata Solis, Director of Human Resources, served via e-service (transaction 41829344). The deposition will take place at our offices and will be recorded stenographically and by video.
note: A deposition of the client's witness, on the tracker with its date.

subject: Brightline document production, volume 2
body: We have uploaded Brightline's second production volume to the shared site, Bates BRT004411 through BRT009872, together with a privilege log for the withheld items.
note: A production to review and log. No window runs against the firm.

subject: Okonkwo: Requests for Admission, Set One
body: Attached are Defendant's Requests for Admission, Set One, served by e-service today. Under Rule 36, each matter is admitted unless a written answer or objection is served within 30 days after being served.
note: Requests for admission, the clock stated in the rule's own words.

subject: Deficient responses to RFP Set Two
body: Marlow's responses to Plaintiff's Requests for Production, Set Two, remain deficient: requests 4, 9 and 11 are answered with boilerplate objections and no documents. Please provide supplemental responses no later than September 25 or let me know times this week to meet and confer. Otherwise we will move to compel.
note: A deficiency letter that demands a meet and confer: discovery and opposing counsel both.

subject: Notice of Deposition of Gail Vance
body: Please find attached the Notice of Deposition of Gail Vance, individually and as person most qualified for Vance Holdings LLC. The deposition will proceed on October 6, 2026 at 9:30 a.m. The deponent is to produce the documents in Attachment A at the deposition.
note: The client's own deposition, with documents to produce: a clock. Its date is written as 'will proceed on October 6', which the parser does not read, so the managing partner sets it.

subject: E-service: Delgado v. Marlow Foods, Deposition Subpoena to Keystone Payroll
body: You are receiving this e-service notification for Case 25-CV-11862. Document served: Deposition Subpoena for Production of Business Records to Keystone Payroll Services. Production date: October 12, 2026. Any objection must be served within ten (10) days of this notice.
note: A records subpoena to a third party that holds the client's payroll data. The objection window is the clock.

subject: Okonkwo: third-party deposition of Dr. Samuel Ortega
body: Notice is given that Defendant will take the deposition of Dr. Samuel Ortega, Plaintiff's treating physician, at the Harborview Medical Building on October 22, 2026 at 1:00 p.m.
note: A third-party deposition the firm attends but does not produce for. A calendar entry, not a response clock, so no alert; it still needs logging, so high.

subject: Re: Re: RFA responses and the mediation
body: Following up on my note last week. Your client's responses to Tillery's Second Requests for Admission (e-service 41812275) are still outstanding, and we will not agree to an extension given the mediation date.
note: Opposing counsel refusing an extension on logged discovery. The mediation on October 8 waits on discovery and falls on the response date, so it is urgent.

subject: Re: supplemental production received
body: Thanks, we received Marlow's supplemental production on the first set of document requests (e-service 41720983). We will be in touch if anything is missing.
note: Names a tracker item that is already closed, so no alert and no unlogged flag. An acknowledgement, not a new request.

subject: FW: Keystone subpoena, client question
body: Jordan, Renata called about the Keystone Payroll subpoena. She wants to know whether Marlow has to tell Keystone anything. Can you call her today?
note: Team mail about a subpoena that already arrived as its own message.

subject: Sunbury: tolling agreement extension
body: Naomi, Kettleman is willing to extend the tolling agreement another sixty days if Sunbury will do the same for its counterclaims. We would need a signed extension before October 15. Let me know and I will circulate a draft.
note: The tolling agreement is a limitations clock. The expiry itself is the next thing on the matter's calendar and it waits on opposing counsel, so it is urgent.

subject: Tillery's offer to compromise
body: Attached is Tillery Construction's statutory offer to compromise, served by e-service (transaction 41868815). The offer remains open for the statutory period. We think it is a sensible number given where the case is.
note: A statutory offer with an expiry on the docket. Mediation waits on discovery, not on this, so the date alone sets the priority.

subject: Re: Re: protective order draft
body: Attached is our redline. We accepted your attorneys' eyes only tier but need the clawback language back in.
note: A threaded reply: opposing counsel's second turn on the draft.

subject: Sunbury Orchards demand
body: I write on behalf of Kettleman Cold Storage in response to your September 2 letter. Kettleman rejects the demand in full and disputes that the compressor failure was its responsibility under the lease. Please direct all further communications to me.
note: A position letter from the other side. Nothing owed by a date.

subject: Early mediation?
body: Jordan, Brightline would consider an early mediation with a private neutral. Is your client open to it? We would want it done ahead of the case management conference.

subject: Courtesy copy: Brightline's Motion to Strike
body: As a courtesy, attached is Brightline's Motion to Strike Portions of the First Amended Complaint, filed and served today. The hearing is set for November 12. Happy to discuss if you think any of it can be resolved without the court.
note: A friendly courtesy copy, but a motion filed and served starts the opposition clock. The message gives no due date, so a person sets it from the hearing date.

subject: Signed stipulation, thanks
body: Thanks for turning the stipulation around so quickly. For your calendar, the order on it requires the amended cross-complaint answer to be filed by October 2.
note: A thank-you note with the clock in its last sentence.

subject: Re: Delgado deposition logistics
body: We can produce Ms. Delgado on September 30 as noticed, but she needs to finish by 3 pm for childcare. Can you confirm you will keep it to one day?
note: Deposition logistics that ask for an answer: discovery and opposing counsel both. The deposition is on the calendar already; no response window.

subject: Mediation prep
body: What do I need to bring to the mediation, and will you need me the day before to prepare? I am travelling the first week of October.
note: A first ask about a scheduled event.

subject: Any word from Kettleman?
body: Has Kettleman's lawyer said anything about extending the agreement? The harvest crew asks me every week whether we are suing.

subject: Re: Re: my deposition transcript
body: Did the transcript from my deposition come back yet? I would like to read it before anything else happens.
note: A threaded reply, the third turn.

subject: Trial budget
body: I am still waiting on the budget through trial that we discussed in August. My partners want to see it before the mediation.
note: The client says she is still waiting: a repeat ask.

subject: October 20 conference
body: Do I need to be at the conference on October 20, or is that just for the lawyers?
note: A date in the question, not a clock.

subject: Re: Re: deposition prep
body: Checking which day works for my deposition prep. Mornings are best for me.
note: A threaded reply, asked before.

subject: FW: subpoena from Barrow Employment Law
body: Keystone Payroll forwarded this to us this morning. It is a subpoena for Ms. Delgado's pay records and says they have to produce within 15 days. Do we need to do anything? It looks routine to me.
note: The client asks a routine question; the window is quoted in passing inside a forward. Counted from the day the client forwarded it, which is the only date the message gives.

subject: Letter from the court
body:
I got this letter from the court in the mail today. It says there is a hearing on November 4. Do I need to go?

---- scanned text ----
NOTICE: The hearing on Plaintiff's Motion for Leave to File a First Amended Complaint is continued to November 4, 2026 at 9:00 a.m.
note: A court notice arriving through the client, with a question of his own. Two topics; a hearing is not a clock.

subject: My brother's case
body: I am Marcus Okonkwo's brother. He asked me to find out whether his case against Brightline is settling. He is working nights and cannot call.
note: Someone writing for the client, not the client. It is still the client's update request, matched by the case name; what may be said to a third party is the attorney's call.

subject: Update
body: It has been five weeks since anyone from your office called me about my case. I do not know what is happening.
note: A repeat chase written without any of the usual repeat words. Code reads it as a first ask.

subject: Settlement number for the lender
body: Our lender needs to see the likely settlement range before October 2 to close the refinance. Where are we on a number?
note: The client's own business date, not a clock the firm answers to. A date parser sees a deadline here; the label says no alert.

subject: Lease review for our second location
body: We are about to sign a lease for a second bakery location and the landlord's form is 40 pages. Do you review commercial leases, and what would it cost?
note: A new matter with no clock.

subject: Referral: slip and fall
body: Naomi, I have a potential client who fell at a grocery store on October 3, 2024 and has a broken wrist. I do not handle injury cases. The two-year period is getting close, so she needs someone to look at it soon. Can I give her your number?
note: A referral with a limitations period running out, but the message gives the incident date, not the deadline. A person sets it.

subject: Served with a lawsuit
body: A process server handed me a summons and complaint from a former business partner. The papers say I have to respond by October 10. Can you help?
note: A prospective client already sued, with the answer date stated.

subject: Non-compete question
body: I have an offer from a competitor and my current employment agreement has a two-year non-compete. Could someone review it before I accept?

subject: 3-day notice from my landlord
body: My landlord taped a notice to my shop door saying I must pay or leave within 3 days. The rent was late because the landlord shut off the water for a week. What can I do?
note: A notice with a three-day window, quoted by the person who received it.

subject: Right to sue letter
body: The EEOC sent me a right-to-sue letter dated September 8 on my discrimination charge. It says I have 90 days to file in court. I need a lawyer.
note: A federal filing window stated from the letter's date. Code does not count from a date inside the message, so a person sets it.

subject: Message for Hale & Marrow: new caller
body: Caller: Howard Tse. Re: dispute with his business partner over the sale of their restaurant. Wants a call back about representation. Best time after 4 pm.
note: A new-matter inquiry that arrives through the answering service, not from the person.

subject: You helped us before
body: You handled our contractor dispute in 2023. Now a general contractor is refusing to pay retainage on a school job and I would like you to take it.
note: A former client with a new problem: a new matter, not a client update. Conflicts first.

subject: Wage claim
body: My employer has not paid me overtime for about eighteen months. I still work there. Is it worth talking to a lawyer?
note: Unpaid overtime with the job ongoing: the limitations period runs back from whenever suit is filed, not toward a date. No clock to set yet.

subject: Invoice CR-22871: Solis deposition transcript
body: Invoice CR-22871 for the certified transcript and rough draft of the deposition of Renata Solis, Delgado v. Marlow Foods. Amount due $1,284.50.

subject: IOLTA account statement available
body: Your August statement for account ending 4471 (Attorney Trust Account) is available in online banking.
note: A trust account statement for the monthly reconciliation.

subject: Retainer replenishment sent
body: Kevin, I wired the $15,000 replenishment to your trust account this morning. Please confirm when it lands.
note: A trust deposit from the client: billing, not an update request.

subject: Invoice SD-1093: hosting, August
body: Monthly hosting and processing charges for the Okonkwo review database, 38 GB. Amount due $912.00.

subject: Second notice: invoice CR-22419
body: Our records show invoice CR-22419 for the Okonkwo deposition remains unpaid after 60 days. Please remit at your earliest convenience.
note: A past-due notice is still billing.

subject: Question about my bill
body: My statement shows 3.2 hours on September 2 for document review. I thought my costs were covered by the contingency agreement. Can someone explain?
note: The client, but the question is about his invoice: billing, not a case update.

subject: Invoice: Vance Holdings v. Tillery mediation
body: Attached is the invoice for the full-day mediation. Per our ADR agreement, fees are due by October 1 to hold the date.
note: A date on a bill is somebody's calendar, not a response clock.

subject: Courtesy notice: account ending 4471
body: The Trust Account Program has received a report from First Harbor Bank of an item presented against insufficient funds on your client trust account. This notice is a courtesy and no finding has been made. Please provide a written explanation and supporting records within fifteen (15) days of the date of this notice.
note: Reads as a courtesy, and trust account items usually go to billing. It is a regulator asking for a written explanation on a window.

subject: Retainer for rebuttal report
body: Before we begin the rebuttal analysis in Okonkwo, we will need a further retainer of $7,500. Our W-9 is attached.

subject: Never miss a deadline again
body: Automatic court rules calendaring for 3,000 jurisdictions. Book a 15-minute demo this week.

subject: You've been nominated: 2027 Top Litigators
body: Congratulations! Your firm has been nominated for our 2027 Top Litigators edition. Confirm your profile to be included in print and online.

subject: Non-recourse capital for your contingency docket
body: We fund single cases and portfolios from $50,000. No recovery, no repayment. Reply to talk to an underwriter.

subject: Contract document reviewers available now
body: Licensed reviewers on 48 hours' notice, remote or onsite. Rates from $55 an hour.

subject: Exclusive employment law leads in your county
body: Pre-screened wrongful termination and wage claim leads delivered to your inbox. Only three firms per county.
note: Sells new-matter leads; a pitch, not an inquiry.

subject: Register by October 2 for early-bird pricing
body: Join 400 litigators in the spring for two days of trial technology sessions. Register by October 2 to save $300.
note: A dated phrase parses in a pitch. A pitch's date is not a clock, so there is no alert.

subject: NOTICE OF PENDING DEFAULT: action required
body: Our records indicate your firm has not updated its attorney registration profile. Failure to respond may result in default status. Click here to update your listing for a one-time fee of $395. This is not a government agency.
note: A pitch dressed as a court notice, down to the capitals. The last sentence says so.

subject: Invoice #LP-7781: annual listing renewal
body: Amount due: $649.00 for your 2027 listing in the Legal Pages Annual. This is a solicitation for the order of goods or services and not a bill. You are under no obligation to pay unless you accept this offer.
note: A solicitation formatted as an invoice. It says it is not a bill.

subject: Summaries of every deposition in minutes
body: Upload a transcript and get a page-line summary before lunch. Your first three transcripts are free.

subject: Is your professional liability renewal coming up?
body: Small firms are switching and saving an average of 18 percent. Get a no-obligation quote in ten minutes.

subject: Your September 30 deposition in Delgado
body: We saw the deposition noticed in Delgado v. Marlow Foods. We can cover it with a realtime reporter and videographer at a 15 percent first-booking discount.
note: A pitch that names a real matter and a real date from a public docket. Still a pitch.

subject: Your e-signature plan: upgrade offer ends Friday
body: Upgrade to the Firm plan before Friday and get unlimited envelopes for the price of your current plan.
note: A weekday date parses in a pitch: somebody's sale, not a clock.

subject: Webinar: trust accounting without spreadsheets
body: Join our free webinar on three-way trust reconciliation for small firms. Seats are limited.

subject: Fall litigation section mixer
body: Join fellow litigators for drinks and a panel on the new discovery rules. Tickets $45, members $30.

subject: Partner meeting moved
body: Moving Tuesday's case review to 8:30 so Jordan can make the Delgado prep. Same room.

subject: Timesheets
body: Reminder that September timesheets are due Friday. I can't send the Vance Holdings bill until everyone is in.
note: A date in team mail is the team's calendar, not a response clock.

subject: Conflicts: Derek Hollins
body: Conflicts check on Derek Hollins came back clear. Naomi, do you want to take the call or should I schedule him with Jordan?

subject: Coverage Thursday afternoon
body: I am in the Solis prep Thursday afternoon. Ines, can you take any calls from Marcus Okonkwo and tell him I will call Friday morning?

subject: FW: Notice of Reassignment: Case 26-CV-04417
body:
Jordan, we have Ellery now. Do we want to use the challenge? Let's talk Monday.

---- Forwarded ----
A party who has not exercised a peremptory challenge may do so within fifteen (15) days of service of this notice.
note: The managing partner forwarding a clock that already arrived as its own notice. The forward is team mail, not a second clock; counting from the forward would also give the wrong date.

subject: Vance RFA responses draft
body: Jordan, first draft of the RFA responses for Vance (41812275) is in the matter folder. Naomi wants them out a week ahead of the mediation.
note: Team mail that names an open tracker item. The docket join corroborates a clock even though nothing new arrived, so code raises an alert the label does not.

subject: Brisco referral
body: Lila, Tom Brisco is sending over a slip and fall. Please open a conflicts check when she calls and flag it to Naomi; the timing is tight.

subject: Good seeing you today
body: Jordan, good to see you at the bar lunch. By the way, our Second Requests for Admission went out by mail on Friday, so you know the drill on timing. Happy to give you an extra week if you ask.
note: A friendly note with discovery served in passing. Unanswered admissions are deemed admitted, so the clock is real; the note never states a date, so a person sets it from the mailing date.

subject: FW: letter from Kettleman's lawyer
body:
Naomi, this came to me directly instead of to you. Is that allowed?

---- Forwarded ----
From Victor Szabo: Mr. Pruitt, Kettleman proposes a meeting of principals to discuss resolving the lease dispute without counsel.
note: Opposing counsel's letter arriving through the client, who also asks a question. Two topics, no clock.
